1.title: Short Term Accommodation Licensing and Penalties

motion_texts.string: That on recommendation of the Deputy City Manager, Housing and Community Growth, the following actions be taken with respect to the staff report, dated March 9, 2026, related to Short-Term Accommodation Licensing and Penalties:
a)     a public participation meeting BE HELD on March 9, 2026, with respect to the proposed by-law amendments for Short-Term Accommodation regulation, as appended to the above-noted staff report;

b)     the proposed by-law, as appended to the above-noted staff report, BE INTRODUCED at the Municipal Council meeting on March 31, 2026, for the purpose of amending Schedule 21 of the City of London Business Licensing By-law - L.-131-16 to improve regulation of Short-Term Accommodation Providers and Brokers;

c)     the proposed by-law, as appended to the above-noted staff report, BE INTRODUCED at the Municipal Council meeting on March 31, 2026, for the purpose of amending the Fees and Charges By-law A-60 to increase the Short-Term Accommodation Provider licence fee; and,

d)     the proposed by-law, as appended to the above-noted staff report, BE INTRODUCED at the Municipal Council meeting on March 31, 2026, for the purpose of amending the Administrative Monetary Penalty System By-law A-54 to increase Administrative Monetary Penalty amounts for Short-Term Accommodation violations;
it being noted that the communications, as appended to the Added Agenda, from M. Hojati, J. Klassen, C. Martin and T. Nguyen, with respect to this matter, were received;
it being pointed out that the following individual a made a verbal presentation at the public participation meeting held in conjunction with this matter:
-    J. Klassen;

it being further noted that, notwithstanding the adoption of this motion, the Community and Protective Services Committee may, at a future time, request a staff report on the additional matter of imposing minimal distance requirements with respect to this matter.
Motion to open the public participation meeting.
Motion to close the public participation meeting.
That the motion BE AMENDED to add a new part that reads as follows:

Notwithstanding the adoption of this motion, the Community and Protective Services Committee may at a future time request a staff report on the additional matter of imposing minimal distance requirements with respect to this matter
That part b) BE AMENDED to read as follows:

the proposed by-law, as appended to the above-noted staff report, to be introduced at the Municipal Council meeting on March 31, 2026, to amend By.-law No. L.-131-16 BE AMENDED in section 8.12 to offer or provide Short-term Accommodation at a Dwelling Unit for more than two individuals per bedroom (not including children under 2 years). Single-room STAS occupant limits will be determined upon inspection but are excluded from this clause
That the motion, as amended, BE APPROVED.

attachments.title: 2026-03-09 SR Short Term Accomodation Licensing and Penalties

1.title: Request to Expedite the Review of the Property Standards By-law CP-24 as it Pertains to Property Conditions that Enable Rat Infestations

motion_texts.string: That the following actions be taken with respect to the communication, dated February 27, 2026, from Councillor H. McAlister, with respect to a Request to Expedite the Review of the Property Standards By-law CP-24 as it Pertains to Property Conditions that Enable Rat Infestations:

a)    the Civic Administration BE DIRECTED to expedite the review the Property Standards By-law- CP-24, as it pertains to property conditions that enable rat infestations, and report back to a future meeting of the Community and Protective Services Committee with potential recommendations to strengthen the enforcement of the by-laws by the end of Q2 2026, with a particular focus on mitigating the risk of rodent infestation; it being noted that this would include all residential property types and not be restricted to just dumpsters;
b)    the Civic Administration BE DIRECTED to include the option to report rat infestation conditions through the Service London portal;
c)    the above-noted communication BE RECEIVED; and,

d)    the Civic Administration BE DIRECTED to consult with the Environmental Stewardship and Action Community Advisory Committee about the City's response to rodent infestations and opportunities for improving public information;
it being noted that verbal delegations from R. Shields and A.M. Valastro, with respect to this matter, were received.
That the requests for delegation status from R. Shields and A.M. Valastro, as appended to the Added Agenda, BE APPROVED.
That the motion BE AMENDED to add a new part d) to read as follows:

The Civic Administration BE DIRECTED to consult with the Environmental Stewardship and Action Community Advisory Committee about the City's response to rodent infestations and opportunities for improving public information.
That part a) BE AMENDED to read as follows:

the Civic Administration BE DIRECTED to expedite the review the Property Standards By-law- CP-24, as it pertains to property conditions that enable rat infestations, and report back to a future meeting of the Community and Protective Services Committee with potential recommendations to strengthen the enforcement of the by-laws by the end of Q2 2026, with a particular focus on mitigating the risk of rodent infestation; it being noted that this would include all residential property types and not be restricted to just dumpsters;
That the motion, as amended, BE APPROVED
That the Committee recess at this time, for 5 minutes.

attachments.title: 2026-03-09 Sub. Dumpsters in Residential Areas - Refuse and Rats - H. McAlister

motion_texts.string: That, pursuant to section 27.6 of the Council Procedure By-law, a change in order of the Community and Protective Services Committee Agenda BE APPROVED, to provide for Item 5.2 in Stage 5, Deferred Matters/Additional Business, to be considered before Item 5.1.
That the following actions be taken with respect to Community Housing Financial Challenges:

a)    the Civic Administration BE DIRECTED to report back to a future meeting of the Community and Protective Services Committee with a summary of the number of units currently vacant within the community housing system in the Service Manager area and collect additional data from community housing providers and provide an analysis of the key factors contributing to the vacancies;

b)    the following actions BE TAKEN with respect to this matter because the committee is concerned that the current conditions constitute a threat to the health and safety to the residents of Tolpuddle and request that the matter of treating the deficiencies to be an emergency which would warrant immediate action:

i)         the Civic Administration BE DIRECTED to immediately advance the funds and approvals necessary for the 2025-2026 COCHI Projects (security system, fire monitoring system) for Tolpuddle Housing Co-operative as outlined in Appendix G of the Feb 17, 2026 Community and Protective Services Committee Item 2.5 Affordable and Community Housing Update as approved projects and without any conditions regarding a lien payment; and,

ii)         the Civic Administration BE DIRECTED to report back to the Community and Protective Services Committee meeting on April 13, 2026 on the lien situation regarding Tolpuddle Housing Co-operative including the amount, any concerns regarding the amount, supports to be offered and a timeline;
it being noted that the following items, with respect to this matter, were received:
That the request for delegation status from J. Phoenix, as appended to the Added Agenda, BE APPROVED.
That, pursuant to section 32.5 of the Council Procedure By-law, “shall the ruling of the Chair BE SUSTAINED?”
That the motion BE AMENDED to add a new part that reads as follows:

The committee is concerned that the current conditions constitute a threat to the health and safety to the residents of Tolpuddle and request that the mater of treating the deficiencies to be an emergency which would warrant immediate action and that the following actions BE TAKEN:

i)         the Civic Administration BE DIRECTED to immediately advance the funds and approvals necessary for the 2025-2026 COCHI Projects (security system, fire monitoring system) for Tolpuddle Housing Co-operative as outlined in Appendix G of the Feb 17/26 CPSC 2.5 Affordable and Community Housing Update as approved projects and without any conditions regarding a lien payment;

ii)         the Civic Administration BE DIRECTED to report back on the lien situation regarding Tolpuddle Housing Co-operative including the amount, any concerns regarding the amount, supports to be offered and a timeline to the April 13, 2026 CPSC.
The motion be further amended to add a new part that reads as follows:

x)         the Civic Administration BE DIRECTED to provide the following details based on the 2024 data used in Appendix B of the staff report, dated February 17, 2026, entitled “Affordable and Community Housing Update”, to the Community and Protective Services Committee:
That the motion, as amended, BE APPROVED.

1.title: (ADDED) Request to Update Municipal Compliance By-law - Amendment to Section 4.7 and Creation of a Public Rental Licence Lookup Tool

motion_texts.string: That the following actions be taken with respect to the communication, dated March 5, 2026, from Councillor C. Rahman, related to a Request to Update the Municipal Compliance By-law and an Amendment to Section 4.7 and Creation of a Public Rental Licence Lookup Tool:

a)    the Civic Administration BE DIRECTED to report back to a future meeting of the Community and Protective Services Committee with proposed amendments to section 4.7 of the Municipal Compliance Services Policy, including options that would permit the City of London to provide complaint status information where appropriate;

b)    the Civic Administration BE DIRECTED to report back to a future meeting of the Community and Protective Services Committee with options for implementing a public rental licence lookup tool, using a model similar to that of the City of Brampton; and,
c)    the Civic Administration BE DIRECTED to investigate placing compliance status updates in the property licensing listing available online.
That pursuant to section 33.8 of the Council Procedure by-law, the Committee BE PERMITTED to proceed beyond 6:00 PM.

attachments.title: 2026-03-09 Sub. Update to Municipal Compliance By-law - C. Rahman

motion_texts.string: That the meeting BE ADJOURNED.
